meta.description: Builds and manages DIA spectral libraries as peptide query parameters (precursor m/z, a few fragment m/z plus relative intensities, normalized RT, optional CCS), covering experimental DDA, chromatogram, and in-silico predicted libraries via Koina-served Prosit, AlphaPeptDeep, MS2PIP, and DeepLC, with iRT/CiRT RT calibration, NCE tuning, format conversion (DIA-NN tsv/speclib/parquet, OpenSWATH pqp/TraML, Spectronaut, blib/dlib/elib), and library QC/merge.

scientific_integrity.detail: Tool Taxonomy citations unchanged and genuine; no fabricated DOI/PMID, sample sizes, or efficacy numbers in any of the 5 re-run outputs or the 2 additional re-audit-only inputs.

practice_boundaries.detail: No clinical, diagnostic, or prescriptive content; entirely peptide/spectral data, no patient-facing scope.

methodological_ground.detail: LOWESS-vs-linear CiRT calibration re-verified unchanged (residual SS 0.21 vs 10.91); the fix's new decoy-generation and RT/intensity-prediction guidance is methodologically correct and independently reproduced on fresh peptide sets.

code_usability.detail: examples/build_library.py re-run unmodified from a fresh copy of the worktree, still produces correct output. All 3 new/changed code snippets in SKILL.md (pyteomics fast_mass for decoy generation, deeplc.predict_and_calibrate, ms2pip HCD2019 workaround) ran successfully on peptide sets the fixer did not use.

functional_suitability.note: The one stale code pattern (DeepLC class) flagged in the prior audit is now replaced with the verified-correct deeplc 4.5.0 module-level API throughout SKILL.md, usage-guide.md, and examples/build_library.py.

reliability.note: The prior audit's three biggest undocumented silent-failure modes (OpenSWATH 0-decoy threshold failure, non-deterministic shuffle decoys, ms2pip first-run model download) are now documented with root cause and workaround, each independently reproduced in this re-audit. Remaining gap: Koina InferenceServerException on malformed peptide input is still not anticipated (unchanged from prior audit, P2).

performance_context.note: SKILL.md grew from 232 to ~291 lines to accommodate the fix; still tight and free of padding, all additions are load-bearing failure-mode documentation.

agent_usability.note: Unchanged from prior audit: very clear, code-exact instructions with strong error-prevention warnings. The new OpenSWATH TSV schema guidance documents 2 of 3 fields actually required for correct multi-peptide conversion (Annotation, real fragment m/z) but omits transition_group_id (new P1 finding, this re-audit).

human_usability.note: Unchanged from prior audit; natural-language quick-start prompts still match real researcher requests.

inputs.note: Core fix independently reproduced on YILAGVENSK/TPVISGGPYEYR (not the fixer's LGGNEQVTR/VEATFGVDESNAK set): placeholder ProductMz + blank Annotation -> 0 decoys / 80% threshold error; real y-ion m/z (pyteomics.mass.fast_mass) + literal Annotation -> 2/2 target/decoy peptides. -method pseudo-reverse confirmed byte-identical (md5-matched) across 5 repeated runs; -method shift confirmed still broken (rejects every peptide as duplicate). recommendations.title: OpenSWATH TSV schema guidance omits transition_group_id
recommendations.problem: A transition list lacking a transition_group_id column (or equivalent unique per-precursor identifier) can have TargetedFileConverter silently merge two distinct peptides that share a PrecursorCharge into a single peptide group -- corrupting target/decoy peptide counts with no error, worse than the now-documented 0-decoy threshold failure because it produces no error at all.
recommendations.root_cause: The fix's new 'OpenSwathDecoyGenerator's real input requirements' section documents the Annotation column and real fragment m/z as the requirements, but the reference OpenSWATH TSV example (and the fixer's own verification data) already included transition_group_id without calling it out as a requirement.
recommendations.fix: Add transition_group_id (unique per PeptideSequence+PrecursorCharge) to the documented required-fields list in 'Convert Library Formats' and the runnable pyteomics snippet, alongside Annotation and real fragment m/z.

recommendations.title: -method reverse's determinism claim is slightly overstated
recommendations.problem: SKILL.md states both -method reverse and -method pseudo-reverse are deterministic ('confirmed byte-identical across repeated runs'). Independent re-testing found pseudo-reverse fully byte-identical across 5 runs, but reverse differed in 1 of 5 runs by a last-ULP floating-point value in a non-scored isolation-window metadata field (not the decoy peptide sequence or fragment content).
recommendations.root_cause: The fix's own verification diffed only 2 runs of each method, which was not enough to catch an intermittent (1-in-5) floating-point discrepancy.
recommendations.fix: Soften the reverse claim (note it is deterministic for decoy peptide/fragment content but has been observed to vary in a metadata-only field) and recommend pseudo-reverse as the primary example when exact reproducibility matters, keeping reverse as a secondary option.

recommendations.title: No input-validation guidance before submitting peptides to Koina
recommendations.problem: Submitting a peptide with a non-standard residue or an unusually long sequence to Koina still raises an uncaught InferenceServerException rather than a Skill-anticipated, user-facing message. Unchanged from the prior audit; not addressed by this fix.
recommendations.root_cause: The Skill does not mention validating peptide sequences (standard 20-AA alphabet, reasonable length) before calling an external prediction service.
recommendations.fix: Add a one-line tip recommending a basic peptide-sequence sanity check (alphabet, length) before submission, with a pointer to catch and report InferenceServerException clearly.
